title: When the community disappoints
hookLine: people fail, the faith is still the faith
tomorrow: Dadi's stopped eating. is sadness a faith problem?

cards: A group chat posts a du'a request for someone in the hospital. Heart emojis pile up under it. Then a week of visiting hours, and almost nobody walks through the door.

That kind of week makes people want to quit a community altogether, quietly, no announcement. Inside the tradition, there are two serious answers to that urge, and both come from the Prophet ﷺ himself.

teach.b: The first answer: stay, and bear it. In Tirmidhi, the Prophet says the believer who mixes with people and patiently bears their harm is better than the one who doesn't mix with them and doesn't bear it.
Communities disappoint; staying anyway isn't foolishness. It's part of the reward. The second answer, at its strongest.
In Bukhari, he says a time will come when the best thing a Muslim owns is a few sheep, which he follows to the mountaintops and the places where rain falls, fleeing with his faith from fitna, trials.

Some scholars read that as room, for some people in some seasons, to step back when the crowd is harming their faith. Others answer that it speaks of real turmoil, not a disappointing week. Notice where the two agree.
Neither one treats the people as the faith.

teach.h: WHERE CAN I SERVE BEST NOW?
teach.b: The jama'a, the community, is people, and people fail. They forget to visit. They judge.
They send hearts instead of coming.
The faith doesn't fail with them, and neither does the One it points to. So the question shifts.
Not is this community worth it, but where can I serve my faith best right now: staying and fixing, or stepping back a season, without stepping back from God.

how: Muslims gather at the masjid for daily and Friday prayers and count visiting the sick as a duty of one Muslim to another; when a community lets them down, many keep praying there while working to make it kinder.

games.q: what does “when the community disappoints” mean?
o: when it's time to leave faith behind for good
when a community's failure proves the faith false
when people of faith let you down, but the faith holds

p: fleeing with your faith in trials

s: the hadith praises the believer who avoids people to stay pure
Tirmidhi: the one who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently is better.
a hadith in Bukhari speaks of fleeing with your faith to the hills in times of trial
some read it as room to step back in a season of real fitna.

games.q: your friend says she's done with her masjid: 'the aunties judge, nobody shows up.' what's the strongest case for HER side, from inside the tradition?
o: a hadith speaks of fleeing with your faith to the hills in times of trial.
the masjid is optional; faith is fine with no community at all.
if the people are bad, that shows the faith itself is bad.
games.why: that's her side at its best. the other side answers with the believer who mixes and bears harm patiently. both agree: the people aren't the faith.

practice: Bring to mind one person from a community that let you down: a masjid, a team, a family group chat. Instead of a complaint, version one small, kind message to them, something like: I'm visiting Thursday, want to come?
You don't have to send it during the sit. Just write it, and read it once.

wordCard.voice: When the community disappoints: people fail, and it's real. The faith is still the faith.

orig.note: Arabic: the community, the gathering; also the congregation in prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: people fail; He doesn't. Stay or step back for a season, but don't step back from Him. Good night.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2507; Sunan Ibn Majah 4032 (the believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently)
Sahih al-Bukhari 19 (sheep on the mountaintops, fleeing with one's religion from trials)
